images.caption: This marker stands on the Appalachian Trail between Mounts Spaulding and Sugarloaf in Maine, in commemoration of the trail's completion by a CCC crew in 1937.  It reads "MAINE C.C.C. In honor of the men of the Civilian Conservation Corps who from 1935-1939 contributed greatly to the completion of the Appalachian Trail in Main and who, on August 14, 1937, near this spot completed the final link of the entire 2,054 mile trail.  Dedicated August 14, 1987 by the volunteers of the Appalachian Trail Club."
images.alt: This marker stands on the Appalachian Trail between Mounts Spaulding and Sugarloaf in Maine, in commemoration of the trail's completion by a CCC crew in 1937.  It reads "MAINE C.C.C. In honor of the men of the Civilian Conservation Corps who from 1935-1939 contributed greatly to the completion of the Appalachian Trail in Main and who, on August 14, 1937, near this spot completed the final link of the entire 2,054 mile trail.  Dedicated August 14, 1987 by the volunteers of the Appalachian Trail Club."

images.caption:
American beech (Fagus grandifolia) sapling along the Appalachian Trail west of Fox Gap, Monroe County.

Beeches retain much of their dead foliage through late autumn into winter, adding much-appreciated texture and color to the otherwise barren woods. The leaf colors range from pale yellow-orange to deep orange.

images.caption:
View from the North Trail, Lehigh Gap Nature Center, Carbon and Lehigh Counties. The trail branches off the Appalachian Trail as it ascends the summit of Blue Mountain.

Toxic metals from nearby zinc smelters destroyed the original vegetation here; however, the nature center has been actively revegetating the area. The sparse tree cover provides sweeping views in all directions.

View from the North Trail, Lehigh Gap Nature Center, Carbon and Lehigh Counties. The trail branches off the Appalachian Trail as it ascends the summit of Blue Mountain.
